title: Define hardware tuning profile schema + validation + versioning strategy
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Define a versioned schema for the “hardware tuning profiles pack” and implement strict validation + guardrails so profiles are safe-by-default across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

This ticket covers:
- Schema definition (keys, types, defaults, optional vs required)
- Versioning/inheritance rules (pack version, profile version, runtime compatibility)
- Validation (static JSON validation + runtime-time sanity checks)
- Deprecation strategy (how we retire keys without breaking old packs)
- Documentation of the schema + a review checklist for adding/modifying knobs

Non-goals
- Implementing the runtime loader / override precedence (tracked in ENG-4823)
- Adding new kernels/scheduler logic; this is about configuration surface + guardrails

Context
We’re shipping curated runtime presets per GPU SKU (H100/B200/L40S) and need a stable interface so:
- Runtime releases can safely consume an external/bundled profile pack
- Private customers can pin a pack version and upgrades don’t silently change behavior
- Perf canaries and oncall can reason about “effective config” deterministically

Proposed artifacts
- JSON schema (or equivalent) checked into runtime repo
- `profiles-pack.json` format with top-level metadata + per-profile config blocks
- Validation library invoked both in CI (lint) and at runtime startup

Links
- Confluence design doc (draft): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/profile-schema-and-compatibility-rules.json
- PR (schema + validation): sources/github/redwood/pr-21984-add-hardware-profile-schema-and-json-validation.json
- Follow-on PRs depend on this surface area

Acceptance criteria
1) Schema:
- Defines pack-level metadata: `pack_version`, `schema_version`, `created_at`, `author`, `description`, `release_channel` (stable/experimental), `runtime_compat`.
- Defines profile-level metadata: `profile_id`, `profile_version`, `gpu_sku`, `maturity` (stable/experimental), `inherits` (optional), `workload_envelope` (required), `notes` (optional).
- Defines config sections (names may differ, but must exist as top-level grouping keys):
  - `scheduler` (batching/queue/backpressure/prefill-decode fairness)
  - `kernels` (kernel-selection toggles + seq-len buckets where applicable)
  - `memory` (KV cache budgets/limits/fragmentation guardrails)
  - `collectives` (optional; only valid when multi-GPU + NCCL enabled)
  - `cpu_runtime` (threading/pinning/allocator knobs if we choose to expose)
- All knobs have explicit types + allowed ranges/enums; any unknown key is rejected in “strict” mode.

2) Versioning + compatibility:
- `schema_version` is semver and governs JSON shape/validation.
- `pack_version` is semver and governs behavioral changes for ops/change management.
- Runtime declares supported `schema_version` range (min/max) and logs compatibility at startup.
- Profiles may inherit from a base profile; inheritance is single-parent, acyclic, and merged deterministically (child overrides parent).
- Deprecation: keys can be marked deprecated with `deprecated_since` and `removed_in` (schema-level), and validation provides warnings for deprecated keys for at least 1 minor runtime release before hard rejection.

3) Validation + guardrails:
- CI validation: a command (or test) that validates the pack(s) committed to the repo; fails on schema violations.
- Runtime validation: on startup, validates selected profile and fails closed to “safe defaults” (or a known baseline profile) when pack/profile is invalid; emits a clear error and a metric/event.
- Guardrails include:
  - Hard caps on batch size / queue depth when `gpu_sku` is L40S (OOM prevention)
  - Disallow `collectives` section unless runtime is in multi-GPU mode and NCCL supported
  - Require `workload_envelope` fields that explain intended usage (e.g., max context, typical concurrency, streaming/non-streaming)

4) Documentation:
- Schema reference is published (in Confluence or in-repo docs), includes examples for H100 and L40S.
- Includes a reviewer checklist for adding any new knob to the schema.

Review checklist (must be pasted into PRs that touch the schema)
- [ ] New key has explicit type + constraints (range/enum) and default behavior is safe.
- [ ] Key is scoped correctly (pack-level vs profile-level vs per-section) and named consistently.
- [ ] Key has a documented failure mode (what happens if too high/low).
- [ ] Key has an owner (Kernels vs Scheduling vs Memory) and at least one reviewer from that area.
- [ ] Any knob that may impact tail latency has a note in `workload_envelope.tradeoffs`.
- [ ] Any knob that can cause OOM has a guardrail tied to GPU SKU memory class.
- [ ] Backward compatibility considered: if changing meaning, bump `pack_version` minor/major and document.
- [ ] Runtime compatibility updated (supported schema range) and startup logs still render correctly.
- [ ] Tests updated/added: positive (valid pack) + negative (invalid key/type/out-of-range).

Notes / decisions to confirm during implementation
- Whether we represent constraints in JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) vs a custom validator (leaning JSON Schema + a thin custom layer for cross-field checks).
- How to model `workload_envelope`: we want enough structure for docs and guardrails, without turning this into a full SLO spec.
- Exact fail-closed behavior: should runtime fall back to “baseline” profile or hard fail startup in Private? Current proposal: Hosted/Dedicated fall back + alert; Private default is configurable but strongly recommended to fall back + emit a startup warning.

Owners / reviewers
- DRI: Ethan Park
- Reviewers: Noah Patel (runtime architecture), Omar El-Sayed (memory/KV), Sofia Ivanova (scheduler), Yuki Sato (kernel selection), Quentin Harris (compat/versioning)
comments: 2025-11-05 (Talia Benson): Marking as P0 for runtime-1.18 cut. Loader work (ENG-4823) is blocked on schema surface area being stable enough for integration tests.

2025-11-07 (Ethan Park): Drafted initial schema outline with pack metadata + per-profile sections. Open question: do we allow arbitrary `extra` fields for forward compatibility? My preference is strict-by-default, with an explicit `extensions` namespace if we need it later.

2025-11-08 (Noah Patel): +1 strict mode. For forward-compat we can do schema_version range checks and ship runtime support before pack updates. Also request: runtime must log both selected profile + schema_version to simplify Private misconfig triage.

2025-11-11 (Omar El-Sayed): Please ensure memory section includes both (a) KV cache budget as a fraction of HBM and (b) hard cap in bytes. L40S experiments show fragmentation sensitivity; we’ll need guardrails that can clamp unsafe values even if pack says otherwise.

2025-11-12 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler knobs should be limited to a curated set. If we expose raw fairness coefficients we will get unreviewable configs. Suggest we allow a small enum for fairness strategy and only a few numeric limits (queue depth, max batch tokens, prefill chunking).

2025-11-14 (Quentin Harris): Versioning proposal: schema_version semver, runtime declares supported range. Pack version separate from schema. Also add `runtime_compat.min_runtime` and `runtime_compat.max_runtime` so pack can explicitly prevent older runtimes from loading it.

2025-11-18 (Ethan Park): Implemented JSON Schema draft + custom cross-field validator (collectives allowed only if multi-gpu; inheritance cycle detection). Added negative tests for unknown keys and out-of-range numeric values.
2025-11-21 (Ethan Park): PR up for review: pr-21984. Includes docs in-repo + example profile snippets. Need final sign-off on fallback behavior wording (Hosted vs Private).

2025-11-25 (Benji Okafor): Confirmed loader integration plan: runtime will validate pack on startup, then validate the selected profile post-override merge. If invalid, fall back to baseline and emit `runtime_profile_validation_failed{reason=...}` metric + structured log event.
2025-12-02 (Noah Patel): Requested change in PR: make inheritance merge order explicit and deterministic (parent first, then child). Also require that `workload_envelope` is present post-merge.
2025-12-10 (Ethan Park): Landed. Follow-ups filed: add more explicit MIG constraints and add doc section on deprecation warnings vs hard failures for Private deployments.
